features.name: repo_trend.py: one trend over all target repos, in the weekly review

features.name: agy hooks really load and run: flat Stop entries, commands anchored to the repo root
features.description: A live agy run (agy -p --mode accept-edits) in a scratch clone of atelier showed no harness hook ever ran. Two bugs. (1) harness_adapter.py wrote agy Stop hooks as a matcher group; agy accepts a group only on tool events, so it rejected the whole .agents/hooks.json ('invalid hook "harness-stop": command hook must specify command') and loaded neither group. (2) agy runs a hook with the folder holding hooks.json (.agents/) as its working directory, so every repo-relative command exited 127, which agy logs and ignores. The harness repo's own .agents/hooks.json had (2) since f43ab92 (2026-10-09) dropped 'cd ..' after testing from the repo root; agy logs show its guards exiting 127 on 2026-10-10 and 10-11.
acceptance_criteria: agy Stop hooks are written as a flat list of hooks; tool events keep the matcher group
every generated agy and codex command reaches agent-hook.sh when run from .agents/ or .codex/
a live agy run in a synced clone runs the edit and Stop hooks from the repo root and gets the sh-check block
the harness repo's own .agents/hooks.json resolves from .agents/
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.evidence: Tests changed first and failed: the two shape assertions (KeyError on the flat Stop) and test_agent_commands_run_from_the_folder_holding_their_hooks_file (exit 127 from .agents/); 34 passed after the fix. Agy and codex commands now start with cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && ; codex's hook working directory is not observed (codex not installed), the prefix is harmless if it already is the root. Live agy 1.4.0 runs in a scratch clone of atelier: before, cli.log 'Failed to parse hooks file ... invalid hook "harness-stop"' and no hook ran; after the shape fix, all hooks exited 127; after both, a logging line in the clone's agent-hook.sh recorded 6 edit and the Stop hooks with the repo root as PWD, and agy reported sh-check's shellcheck block (SC1072/SC1073). The earlier replay test in feat-080 ran the commands from the repo root and so could not see either bug. The clone's Stop also showed atelier's secret-scan.sh blocking on existing osv-scanner advisories in apps/firstdigital/package-lock.json, true on the real atelier too (rc 2 on a clean tree); not fixed here. The fixture telemetry dir it wrote was removed. harness-verify.sh: all 11 gates passed, output saved to a file.

features.name: Global hooks for every repo; a repo hook of the same name wins
features.description: T13 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-two-layer-harness-design.md, decisions D10 and D11. templates/hooks/global/global-hook.sh <claude|agy|codex> <edit|stop|start> runs sh-check (edit), secret-scan (Stop) and preflight (Claude SessionStart, only where PROGRESS.md or agent-harness.json exists) in the repo the agent works in. It finds the repo from the hook input (the edited file, else cwd, else agy's workspacePaths), because agy runs global hooks in ~/.gemini/config. A repo whose .claude/settings(.local).json, .agents/hooks.json or .codex/hooks.json names the same hook keeps its own, so nothing runs twice and repo config blocks still apply. install.sh copies it and the hooks it runs to <runtime>/hooks/ (runtime_files, so the drift gate covers them) and merges `harness_adapter.py global-wiring` per agent into ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json and ~/.codex/hooks.json; uninstall.sh removes them.
acceptance_criteria: the dispatcher runs each hook in the repo root found from claude, agy and codex input, run from an unrelated folder
a hook the repo wires itself is skipped; start is silent without PROGRESS.md or agent-harness.json
global wiring per agent: matcher per agent, agy Stop flat, SessionStart only for claude; merged once next to existing hooks, removed alone
live: Claude and agy edit hooks block a broken .sh in a repo with no hooks of its own; agy Stop blocks on a planted fake token
hangar, atelier and agent-skills-setup skip the global secret-scan (they wire their own)

features.name: Weekly harness evaluation of every target repo, silent unless worse
features.description: Nothing ran update.sh or the repo audits on a schedule, so a newly installed agent, a drifted hook or a failing verify surfaced only by hand. scripts/harness_weekly.py takes update.sh's output and exit code, audits each registered repo into <runtime>/audits/<repo>/<date>.json (per machine: committing here would break update.sh's pull --ff-only once the remote moves), compares with the latest earlier audit and writes a markdown report with the repo_trend table. Regressions: update.sh failed; a repo failed to sync; a new outside agent detected (codex once installed) or a listed one not answering; a hook drifted; always-loaded tokens up more than 10%; a repo's latest verify run failed. Exit 1 on regressions, 2 on no verdict. hangar's scripts/jobs/harness-weekly.sh (LaunchAgent top.firstdigital.harness-weekly, Monday 09:30) runs update.sh then this, writes ~/hangar-weekly/harness-<YYYY-Www>.md and sends ntfy only on regressions or no verdict.
acceptance_criteria: each regression class is reported, and a clean week reports none
the latest verify run decides, not an earlier failure
this week's audit is saved per machine and compared with the latest earlier one
exit 1 only on regressions, with the report written either way
the hangar job runs end to end on this host and is silent on a clean week

LaunchAgent bootstrapped (Weekday 1, 09:30). hangar's CronJobNotRunning rule now covers harness-weekly at the weekly threshold. Not exercised: the ntfy path (no regression this week).
